A1.justification: Both complete, readable 24-page PDFs describe the same PRISM study. The main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–B can be matched reliably, including the image-based qualitative examples.

before.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix B report original ALFWorld and R2R evaluations, ablations, training curves, inference measurements and analyses of generated descriptions and questions.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix B, including benchmark performance and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same dynamic question generation, VLM answering, LLM description synthesis and LoRA policy trained with behavioral cloning and PPO. Appendix A's prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six ALFWorld household task categories and R2R navigation coverage. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 1–6 and the appendix analyses. This includes the ALFWorld baselines and ablation variants, and R2R's LangNav, NavGPT, DiscussNAV and marked reimplementations.

E3.justification: The model configurations, training procedures, metrics, checkpoint selection and evaluation splits remain unchanged. Appendix B retains the same episode counts in Table 7 and the 1,000-transition answer-accuracy evaluation.

E4.justification: The architecture, merging-strategy and oracle-question ablations are retained unchanged. Appendix B also preserves the training curves, latency analysis, alternative-backbone evaluation, answer accuracy, question-budget analysis and qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Figures 3 and 6 retain the same p < 0.005 significance annotations, and Figure 7 retains its error bars. No changes to run counts, seeds, uncertainty reporting or statistical procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. Table 1 still reports 77% and 80% average ALFWorld success for PRISM BC and BC+RL, respectively; Table 6 retains 46.08% R2R success. Appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation and Equations 1–7 retain the same definitions, action probabilities and training objectives. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about automatic goal-oriented perception, coupling perception with reasoning, and improved performance on ALFWorld and R2R.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning goal-conditioning hallucinations, oracle environment priors, information synthesis and inference-latency tradeoffs are unchanged. The discussion of extending the approach to lower-level robotic control is also retained.

D1.justification: V2 removes the introduction's 'Code can be found here' footnote and its repository hyperlink without a replacement. Appendix prompts, hyperparameters and hardware details remain unchanged. This establishes a loss of access information, not withdrawal of the repository itself.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and positioning against prior modular agents and question-answering approaches are unchanged. The new proceedings notice does not alter the research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 replaces the preprint notice with an ICML 2026 proceedings and copyright notice and removes the code footnote. Scientific prose, terminology and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There are limited changes to author-line wrapping, spacing, figure sizing and float placement. For example, Table 5 moves from page 7 to page 8. Figures and tables retain their content, labels and captions.

improvement.justification: The scientific content and supporting evidence are unchanged, but removing the sole explicit code-access footnote and repository link modestly weakens reproducibility documentation. The proceedings notice and layout adjustments provide no substantive compensating improvement. This judgment concerns the PDFs' documentation, not the repository's actual availability.
